thread:
Aisha: FYI escalation from BrightCart — their batch /v1/rerank call is returning scores that don't line up with per-query candidate lists. They send 3 queries in one request and the service returns a single flat scores array (or at least that's how their client sees it), so the scores end up applied to the wrong candidates. Customer says this started after last week's runtime deploy. :warning:

Aisha: Repro payload they sent (redacted):
```json
{
  \"queries\": [
    {
      \"q\": \"best wireless earbuds under $100\",
      \"candidates\": [
        {\"candidate_id\": \"c1\", \"text\": \"Earbuds A\"},
        {\"candidate_id\": \"c2\", \"text\": \"Earbuds B\"}
      ]
    },
    {
      \"q\": \"budget bluetooth speakers\",
      \"candidates\": [
        {\"candidate_id\": \"c3\", \"text\": \"Speaker X\"}
      ]
    },
    {
      \"q\": \"noise cancelling headphones\",
      \"candidates\": []
    }
  ]
}
```

Aisha: Their client receives: 3 scores in results but the order is inconsistent with per-query grouping. They included the API response header X-Request-Id: `req_02Gxyz` and said they saw a 200 with body like:
```json
{
  \"scores\": [0.77, 0.41, 0.62],
  \"mapping\": null
}
```

Aisha: They tried adding an explicit `candidate_id` and it still mismatches. Workaround they used: send each query as its own rerank call which works. But they have heavy batch traffic so that's not acceptable due to latency/cost.

Tom: @Aisha thanks. :eyes: can you attach the raw request/response pair from the BrightCart logs (we need the bytes for exact ordering)? Also what sdk/version are they using? We had a change in how batch flattening works in the client lib last week.

Aisha: Uploading logs now — they sent the `raw_request.json` and `raw_response.json` in the ticket. SDK is `redwood-js@1.4.2` (client). They claim they are not using any SDK transformation though, just a direct fetch to /v1/rerank.

ops-bot: New alert: deploy-2026-03-05 changed rerank batch marshaling on runtime nodes. Rollout started 2026-03-05T03:12Z, 100% by 03:27Z. (deployment id: deploy-rl-614)

Jules: tagging in ml-infra. This sounds like the batch->flatten step in the reranker service might be dropping empty candidate buckets or not emitting per-query offsets. My hypothesis: we used to return `per_query_offsets` when candidates vary, but a refactor accidentally switched to returning flat scores only.

Mike: From customer POV, the observed mismatch pattern is consistent: the second query's single candidate got the first score sometimes. When they removed the empty candidate list for the third query (i.e., removed the empty array), mapping looked correct. So empty lists might be shifting offsets.

Tom: Reproduction steps i'm doing locally: 1) run repro harness against staging rerank with the exact payload, 2) curl with `-v` capture raw bytes, 3) check JSON pointer paths. Quick test command I used: 
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d @raw_request.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank?mode=batch
```

Tom: On my staging node I see the response contains `scores` and also `per_query_counts` in some instances but not always. Reproducer attached: `1752001300-repro.zip` (contains request/response).

Jules: Found the suspicious commit in rerank-serializer that touched how we encode `candidates.length==0`. There's an old branch: when candidate list empty we used to insert a placeholder nil so offsets stayed stable; new code drops the placeholder. That would cause a left-shift of later offsets for clients expecting placeholder entries.

Aisha: Customer is concerned about billing — they were billed for the batch request which returned weird scores. Can we confirm cost attribution? They want an adjustment if the output is incorrect.

Mike: @Aisha we should offer an immediate credit and a follow-up once root cause and impact window confirmed. I'll draft a note for support reply.

Tom: Suggested short-term mitigation: accept either format by looking up `candidate_id` when present. But that's a server-side change and might be nontrivial. Shortest patch: have rerank runtime include `per_query_offsets` field in response again (revert the placeholder-dropping behavior) — small change in serializer.

Jules: I'll open a hotfix PR to restore insertion of zero-length markers so offsets are stable and add a regression test that sends mixed empty/non-empty candidate lists. Also adding a test that verifies `scores` length equals sum of candidate counts and that offsets map.

Jules: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/rerank-serializer/pulls/1128 (hotfix) — added tests and explicit `per_query_offsets` in response. Rolling to canary now.

ops-bot: Canary rollout started for rerank-serializer hotfix (canary nodes: 12).

Aisha: I replied to BrightCart with temporary workaround (split into per-query calls or ensure no empty candidate arrays) and offered a billing credit. Customer grateful but wants ETA.

Tom: Canary looks clean for 10 minutes. I'm kicking a full rollout. After rollout we'll backfill a short incident note to customers impacted and open a billing ticket for credits.

Jules: Postmortem todo: 1) add unit tests for empty candidate buckets; 2) add integration test that compares request->response mapping with random candidate counts; 3) add an API contract doc for batch rerank format and explicit examples showing empty lists handling; 4) add an alert when `scores.length != sum(candidates.length)` for any response.

Mike: I'll coordinate credits and the customer follow-up. Support reply includes: short root cause, immediate workaround, ETA for rollback/hotfix, and confirmation of credit.

Aisha: Closing loop — BrightCart confirmed behavior fixed after hotfix rollout and accepted the credit. Closing ticket after final billing adjustment completes. :white_check_mark:
